description: Elements: a tribe can have 1 per 2 levels of Administration (5 at most).
Makes armour (shields, helms, breastplates and more) from coal and bronze or iron.
Makes bone items: axes, spears, arrows, frames and more.
Takes the bones from slaughtered animals: each worker does 6 goats, 3 cattle or 2 horses for 12 bones. Can be combined with Skinning and Gutting.
Turns grain, grapes, honey or gut into provs: each cook makes 4 (6 with grain).
Couriers: +15 MP, can't scout; only one tribe in the clan may hold Courier.
Cures skins or furs into leather: each worker turns 2 into 2 leather using 5 gut.
How many tribes the clan can have: 1 per level of the clan's highest Diplomacy, and new tribes split from the tribe holding it. Dip 7 also gives Fair access.
Dresses skins or furs into leather: each worker turns 4 into 4 leather using 1 salt.
Trade: Economics 5 (or 4 with a Trading Post) lets a tribe trade at the Fair.
Builds structures: a Meeting House (Engineering 2, 100 logs) founds a village; more buildings at higher levels.
Farming crops; village only (needs a Meeting House).
Fishing from a hex with a river, lake or ocean hexside: about 2.5 provs per worker at level 0, the same in every season; +5% a level.
Makes arrows: each worker makes 10 from 10 coal and 1 bronze, iron or steel.
Fells logs or strips bark in forest or jungle: each worker 4 logs or 20 lb of bark. Logs can't be used the turn they're cut. Also covers charcoal making.
A kind of hunting that keeps the hides: fewer provs than hunting, but skins and furs too. The mix depends on the season.
Garrisons: a tribe can have 1 per level.
Makes glass items (beads, beakers and more) from sand, lead, coal and clay.
Takes the gut from slaughtered animals: each worker does 6 goats, 3 cattle or 2 horses for 12 gut. Can be combined with Skinning and Boning.
Heals wounded fighters after combat: one healer per 5 wounded; herbs help. Not entered as an activity.
Herders keep animals together and let them breed: 1 per 10 horses, cattle or dogs, or 20 goats. Unherded animals stray. Skill, season, weather and terrain set the breeding rate.
Gathers provs: game, honey, fruit, roots and berries. The haul depends on hunters, skill, terrain, season and weather; traps and slings help.
Gets information from locals; higher levels unlock more (nearest terrain or ore at 3, Rich Seeking hexes at 4 and 5, special hexes at 6, towns and cities at 9).
Makes trinkets, ornaments, goldwork and inlays; trinkets and ornaments sell at the Fair.
Makes leather goods: hoods, shields, slings, jerkins, backpacks (+30 lb carried), saddlebags, saddles, rope.
Makes metal tools and items from iron (or bronze or brass, with less coal).
Mines a deposit in the unit's hex: coal, ores, salt, silver, gold and more. Miners can die, most of all in winter.
Musical performance (it earns at the Fair) and making instruments, with Woodwork or Metalwork.
Makes ewers, jars and urns from clay and coal.
Quarries stone in hills and mountains: each worker 5 stones (double with mattocks).
Refining ore into metal; village only (needs a Meeting House).
With salt, turns fish into provs that keep.
Doesn't add range: it cuts scout losses (Scouting 6 all but stops them), helps evade Security and raises Seeking returns.
Raises returns from Seeking, the warriors' search for goods, animals and recruits each month 1.
Makes sewn goods: bladders, mail, fur jackets and coats, curtains.
Makes siege equipment: rams, ballistas, onagers, catapults.
Skins slaughtered animals: each worker does 3 goats, 1 cattle or 1 horse (1, 2 or 3 skins each). The animals' provs are gained too.
Handling slaves: slaves work as actives but need overseers (1 warrior per 10 at Slavery 0) or they may flee.
Makes stone items and buildings from quarried stone.
Tans skins or furs into leather using bark: 10 workers per level make 40 leather with 100 bark.
Triball at the Fair (up to 800 warriors) and the month-12 League, both earn silver.
Makes parchment, candles and cuirboilli from wax, skins and cotton.
Makes weapons (shafts, spears, swords, bows and more) from coal and metal.
Makes rope, nets, snares (help fishing), cloth and carpets.
Makes wooden goods: clubs (no logs needed in forest or jungle), paddles, rakes, wagons.
